summary: Spinmons are superconducting qubits formed by entangling a transmon with the spin of a trapped Andreev quasiparticle in a mesoscopic Josephson junction, offering potential simultaneous protection against multiple decoherence channels. Full qubit control is achieved through electrostatic gating and AC flux driving, with computed relaxation rates below 100 Hz and protection against charge noise via operation at a stationary point of qubit frequency.
motivation: Single-degree-of-freedom superconducting qubits face fundamental tradeoffs between protection against relaxation and dephasing; combining macroscopic (transmon) and microscopic (Andreev spin) quantum degrees of freedom offers a route to avoid this tradeoff while leveraging the Franck-Condon blockade for suppression of spin-flip relaxation.
method: The spinmon Hamiltonian combines an odd-parity Josephson junction with spin-orbit coupling (Andreev spin qubit) in parallel with a gate-tunable even-parity junction, shunted by a capacitor. Zeeman field $B \sim E_c = h \times 40$ MHz lifts Kramers degeneracy, enabling control via electric dipole spin resonance ($\Omega_{xx}$ driving) and AC flux ($\Omega$ qubit-flip coupling), computed in the heavy transmon limit where $E_C \ll E_0 \sim E_{SO} \sim E_J$ with $E_0 = E_{SO} = h \times 500$ MHz.
result: Flux noise and charge noise relaxation rates remain below 100 Hz and 10 Hz respectively at idle configuration, excitation rates out of computational subspace below 10 Hz, with protection against dephasing from charge noise since qubit frequency sits at extremum of $\Delta E = E_0 - E_J(V_{g2})$; thermal excitations at $T = 10$ mK limit initialization since $\hbar\omega_q/k_B \ll 1$ K due to small $E_{SO}$.
